title: Cap. 1 vocabulary: Reprobatio effects; against Pelagian calumny (Prosper)
pass_a_gloss: But the proper and true effects of negative reprobation are these: To be unwilling to decree the efficacious liberation of a person lying in the state of damnation; To will to deny to such a person the efficacious helps by which he would in fact be converted. The last effect is the eternal punishment of the obstinate sinner: which does not properly arise from mere passing-by or non-election, but from that other act of reprobation which it is permitted to call pre-damnation; and it presupposes the foreseeing of sin, and dereliction in the same. Now that also must be weighed, that the effects of reprobation do not have that connection among themselves which the effects of predestination have. For in predestination the prior effect is accustomed to be the cause of the posterior; as efficacious calling begets faith, faith justification, etc.; but in reprobation the effects are not ordered to one another in this mode, although all taken jointly are ordered unto one and the same end, namely the shining-forth of Divine justice. Finally, this also must be noticed against the malevolent calumnies of certain ones: Although sins such as unbelief, wickedness, hardening, and the penalty owed to these, that is, eternal damnation, follow reprobation in the fallen human being equally infallibly as faith, holiness, perseverance follow predestination, nevertheless they do not follow in the same mode. For God acting from the decree of predestination works these prior things through the influx of efficacious grace: but from the decree of reprobation he does nothing by which the reprobate is made worse, nothing by which he is either impeded from believing and living holily, or impelled unto unbelief or wickedness. This must carefully be observed, because both the old Pelagians and the new, when they see that, such reprobation as we have described having been posited, none of the reprobate either believe perseveringly or live holily, immediately cry out that we make God the author of sin, and the cause why they either do not believe or spring back from faith and holiness; But with the Prophet we answer to any reprobate, your destruction is from you, although help is from God alone. For reprobation subtracts nothing from the power of the reprobate himself, although God toward him does not put forth that efficacious power which he could if he willed. So formerly Prosper: God despoils no one of the possibility of the good. It is not therefore a consequence, as those think who object such things, that God from those to whom he has not given penitence has taken away repentance; and those whom he has not lifted, he has struck down, etc. — these are his words. Far otherwise therefore does reprobation hold itself in causing than predestination. God predestinating works all goods in the predestined through the influx of grace, and is properly named an efficient cause: but God reprobating works no evils in the reprobate through subtraction of grace, but evils consequently break forth from the corruption of nature, of which God is no more the cause than the sun is of darknesses, when it does not illuminate the air. These things concerning election, Predestination, and reprobation I have thought should be set forth beforehand.
pass_b_english: The proper effects of negative reprobation are these: unwillingness to decree the efficacious liberation of a person lying under damnation; and the will to deny that person the efficacious helps by which he would in fact be converted. The last effect is the eternal punishment of the obstinate sinner. That does not properly rise from mere passing-by or non-election, but from the other reprobation-act one may call pre-damnation — which presupposes foresight of sin and leaving the person in it. Weigh this too: reprobation's effects are not chained to one another the way predestination's are. In predestination the earlier effect usually causes the later — efficacious calling begets faith, faith justification, and so on. In reprobation the effects are not ordered that way, though taken together they serve one end: the shining of Divine justice. Finally, against certain malevolent slanders, mark this: In the fallen human being, sins such as unbelief, wickedness, and hardening — and the penalty due them, eternal damnation — follow reprobation as infallibly as faith, holiness, and perseverance follow predestination; yet they do not follow in the same way. Acting from the decree of predestination, God works those earlier goods by the influx of efficacious grace. From the decree of reprobation he does nothing that makes the reprobate worse, nothing that blocks believing and holy living, nothing that drives him into unbelief or wickedness. Watch that carefully. Old Pelagians and new alike see that, given reprobation as we have described it, none of the reprobate perseveres in faith or holy life — and they cry at once that we make God the author of sin and the cause why people do not believe or spring back from faith and holiness. With the Prophet we answer every reprobate: your destruction is from you, though help is from God alone. Reprobation takes nothing from the reprobate's own power; God simply does not put forth toward him the efficacious power he could put forth if he willed. So Prosper long ago: God despoils no one of the possibility of the good. It does not follow — as the objectors think — that those to whom God has not given penitence he has robbed of repentance, or that those he has not lifted he has struck down, and so on. Reprobation causes in a far different way from predestination. God predestinating works every good in the predestined by grace's influx, and is properly called an efficient cause. God reprobating works no evils in the reprobate by subtracting grace; the evils break out from nature's corruption — and God is no more their cause than the sun is cause of darkness when it does not light the air. So much I thought should be set down first on election, Predestination, and reprobation.
source_text: Propria autem & vera effecta reprobationis negativae haec sunt: Nolle decernere efficacem liberationem personae in statu damnationis jacentis; Velle negare tali personae auxilia efficacia quibus de facto converteretur. Ultimus effectus est aeterna punitio obstinati peccatoris: qui non proprie oritur ex mera praeteritione vel non-electione, sed ex illo altero reprobationis actu, quem praedamnationem licet appellare; atque peccati praevisionem supponit, & derelictionem in eodem. Jam & illud perpendendum, effecta reprobationis non habere illam connexionem inter se, quam habent effecta praedestinationis. Nam in praedestinatione prior effectus solet esse causa posterioris; ut vocatio efficax parit fidem, fides justificationem, &c.; sed in reprobatione effectus non sunt hoc modo invicem ordinati, quamvis omnes junctim sumpti ordinentur ad unum & eundem finem, relucentiam scilicet justitiae Divinae. Ultimo, & illud contra quorumdam malevolas calumniationes animadvertendum est: Licet peccata, qualia sunt infidelitas, improbitas, obduratio, & poena hisce debita, hoc est, aeterna damnatio, in homine lapso aeque infallibiliter consequantur reprobationem, atque fides, sanctitas, perseverantia consequuntur praedestinationem, tamen non eodem modo consequuntur. Nam Deus agens ex decreto praedestinationis operatur haec priora per influxum gratiae efficacis: at ex decreto reprobationis nihil agit quo deterior efficiatur reprobatus, nihil quo vel impediatur a credendo & sancte vivendo, vel impellatur ad infidelitatem aut improbitatem. Hoc diligenter observandum est, quia tam veteres Pelagiani, quam novi, cum videant, posita reprobatione tali qualem descripsimus, neminem reproborum aut credere perseveranter, aut sancte vivere, illico clamant, nos facere Deum autorem peccati, & causam cur vel non credant, vel resilant a fide & sanctitate; Sed cum Propheta respondemus cuivis reprobo, perditio tua ex te, licet auxilium ex solo Deo. Nam reprobatio nil subtrahit de potentia ipsius reprobati, quamvis Deus erga illum non exserat illam potentiam efficacem, quam posset si vellet. Sic olim Prosper, Deus neminem boni possibilitate desoliat. Non est ergo consequens, sicut putant qui talia objiciunt, ut Deus quibus poenitentiam non dederit, resipiscentiam abstulerit; & quos non levaverit, alliserit, &c. haec ille. Longe aliter igitur se habet reprobatio in causando, quam praedestinatio. Deus praedestinans operatur omnia bona in praedestinatis per influxum gratiae, & causa efficiens proprie nominatur: sed Deus reprobans nulla operatur mala in reprobis per subtractionem gratiae, sed mala consequenter erumpunt ex corruptione naturae, quorum Deus non magis causa est, quam sol tenebrarum, quando non illuminat aerem. Haec de electione, Praedestinatione & reprobatione praefanda putavi.
